appStack.description: The application stack name, used for naming resources and grouping applications

canary.description: Canary settings for every application with deploymentType rollout (DEVOPS-311). The chart injects the stable and -preview Services, Istio weights on every VirtualService route that reaches the app, progressDeadlineSeconds with progressDeadlineAbort, and a rollbackWindow of 2 revisions.

preset.description: Step ladder. standard: 10, 25 and 50 with a 5m pause after each, then 100. fast: 25, then 100. manual: 10, then a pause until resumed, then 100. An analysis step follows each weight and runs health (unless analysis.health.enabled is false) and the extra analysis.templates.

stepsOutsideProd.description: Render the canary steps (preset or explicit steps, with their barriers, analysis steps, pauses and dark stage) and mycarrier.tech/canaryBudgetSeconds outside prod, as in prod, for a test drill (DEVOPS-516). The chart's own alerts check stays prod only; in a drill only a replacement alerts entry (applications.<app>.analysisTemplates) runs as background analysis. It applies only to a Rollout whose repository's deployment-strategy property (global.deploymentStrategy) is canary; any other Rollout renders no steps in every environment, with or without it. false: only environment.name prod renders them; elsewhere a canary Rollout renders steps: [] and promotes at once. The render-time checks of a canary Rollout run in every environment either way, the leader rule, the leader's tests-dark, budgetSeconds for explicit steps and the budget limit included; only global.correlationId for the coordinator is required just where the steps render. New after 4.7.9: the 4.7.9 schema refuses it.

manualTimeout.description: How long the release's rollout-watch allows for the manual preset's pause (Tech Spec D22): it counts as this duration in the canary budget (mycarrier.tech/canaryBudgetSeconds). The pause itself has no time limit. With the manual preset, zero fails the render. Ignored by the standard and fast presets and by an explicit steps list.

steps.description: Argo Rollouts canary steps that replace the preset verbatim. Like the preset, they render only for a Rollout whose deployment-strategy property is canary, and only in prod or with stepsOutsideProd; elsewhere such a Rollout renders steps: []. A steps list needs budgetSeconds in every environment, or the render fails.

budgetSeconds.description: The worst-case length of an explicit steps list, in seconds (Tech Spec D22): its pause durations, each analysis step's longest template (count x max(interval, the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds)) and each barrier timeout, added up. Rendered as mycarrier.tech/canaryBudgetSeconds on every canary Rollout whose steps render (prod, or stepsOutsideProd); the release's rollout-watch times out at the largest value of the release plus 15 minutes. Required with steps in every environment, also where they do not render, and the render fails without it. Ignored with a preset: the chart computes the budget from the steps it renders. At most 5700: rollout-watch's release workflow has activeDeadlineSeconds 10800, which also covers about 70 minutes before the canary starts and 15 minutes after the budget; a computed budget above 5700 fails the render too.

enabled.description: Deprecated: canary analysis is mandatory for every Rollout (DEVOPS-312). true is accepted and has no effect; false fails the render in every environment. Remove it; turn off one check with health.enabled or alerts.enabled instead.

templates.description: Extra AnalysisTemplates each analysis step runs together with health, as suffixes of <environment>-<fullName>-; each must render for every Rollout application, or the render fails. The chart renders tests (DEVOPS-515: the application's testtrigger.testdefinitions through TestEngine, see analysis.tests) for an application with testtrigger.testdefinitions; define any other under applications.<app>.analysisTemplates (compare, DEVOPS-322, is not built yet). health and alerts always run unless opted out with health.enabled or alerts.enabled: listing either here fails the render. With health.enabled and alerts.enabled both false, this list must not be empty: analysis is mandatory for every Rollout.

tests.description: The chart's tests template (DEVOPS-515), <environment>-<fullName>-tests, rendered in every environment for each canary Rollout application (global.deploymentStrategy canary; any other Rollout ignores it) when analysis.templates lists tests or explicit steps reference it, unless applications.<app>.analysisTemplates has an entry named tests (it replaces the chart's). A Job sends the application's testtrigger.testdefinitions, the request of its PostSync hook with ServiceAddress the -preview Service, RunKind canary, SlipStep none and Tolerations [], to TestEngine's v1 API and exits 0 only when the run passes; a failed run, a second no_results or infra_failed, TestEngine with RUN_KINDS_ENABLED off, a 5xx or the end of the timeout fails the AnalysisRun and aborts the canary. An application without testtrigger.testdefinitions fails the render, and so do a test definition's serviceAddress whose host is not the application's own Service or its -preview Service, or whose port is not the http Service port (one on it keeps its path on the -preview Service), a -preview Service with no http port, a testtrigger.apikey that is not a vault: reference, managed routes on the Rollout, that is dark: true with the coordinator on or explicit header or mirror routes (TestEngine's DeployVerifier fails a run without the canary header on a Rollout with managed routes), coordinator.enabled false with more than one canary Rollout, and an empty global.correlationId where the steps render.

timeout.description: Poll budget of the tests Job: the whole run, the one resubmit after no_results or infra_failed included. The Job's activeDeadlineSeconds is this plus startupSeconds (540 by default), which the canary budget counts for each analysis step. With the coordinator on and more than one canary Rollout, each analysis step's longest run of one Rollout (its longest template; for a Job, its activeDeadlineSeconds plus ceil(sqrt(2 x activeDeadlineSeconds)) for Argo Rollouts to see it end) minus the shortest of another ((count - 1) x interval of its templates) must stay below the timeout of the barrier after the step, or the render fails. A release with one canary Rollout has no such wait. Zero fails the render.

startupSeconds.description: Slack for the tests Job's pod to start (scheduling, an on-demand node scale-up, the image pull, the Vault injection) before its poll budget begins: the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds is timeout plus this. Kubernetes counts activeDeadlineSeconds from the Job's creation, Pending included, and the pod cannot read its own start time. A pod still Pending past it ends DeadlineExceeded: the Job condition shows it, the script prints no FAIL line, and a TestEngine run already started is left running.

image.description: Image of the tests Job: Python 3 with its standard library. Set it to a mirror of the default image.

health.description: The chart's health template, which each analysis step runs unless enabled is false: it calls the app's -preview Service at canaryHealthPath or health.path on the http port, or else at the httpGet path of the app's liveness probe (probes.livenessProbe, or the global.language default unless probes.enableLiveness is false; csharp defaults to /liveness; readiness and startup probes are not used), reads a JSON body at $.status and evaluates successCondition. The render fails when no path is found. Argo Rollouts up to v1.10.1 counts a 2xx body that is not JSON as Successful without evaluating the condition; argo-rollouts#4770 (merged, not yet released) evaluates it on the raw body instead, so an application whose health path serves HTML needs successCondition "true".

enabled.description: Run the health check in each analysis step. false opts out; analysis.alerts.enabled false as well then needs at least one extra template in analysis.templates, because analysis is mandatory for every Rollout.

successCondition.description: Condition on the value read at $.status (on the raw body when it is not JSON, from argo-rollouts#4770 on). "true" accepts any 2xx answer; a non-2xx answer is an error either way.

path.description: HTTP path the health check calls on each Rollout application's http (or healthcheck) port. Unset: the httpGet path of the application's liveness probe. Set it for an application whose liveness probe is not HTTP (TCP, exec, or turned off).

consecutiveErrorLimit.description: Errors in a row (any non-2xx answer, timeout or connection error) that the check tolerates; one more ends the run as Error, which aborts the canary. The default 1 rides out a single transient error (an error is retried after about 10 s); 0 aborts on the first error.

alerts.description: The chart's alerts template, on unless enabled is false, rendered in prod only (canaries run only in prod) with DEVOPS-329's label contract (alert-gate's matchers). The Rollout runs it as background analysis from its first weight until promotion. Its alert-rules Job runs twice at the start and is never in dry run: it fails the canary when neither run finds an alert rule that can fire (not paused, not in error) for the service label, so the deploy is refused until the rules or the label are fixed, and also on a configuration error (a 401 or 403, another 4xx or a redirect, an empty Vault property, or a pod that cannot start or finish within 360 s); a Grafana outage (a 5xx, a 429, a timeout, a network error or a body that is not JSON, after 3 tries) passes and is logged; an image that cannot be pulled pauses the canary. Its alerts web metric fails when a firing alert that is not silenced carries the service label, the environment (in prod, also no environment label) and a folder other than Platform. Both read the Grafana token from an ExternalSecret on vault-backend-devops (DevOps grafana/service-accounts/api/tokens).

enabled.description: Run the alerts check as background analysis (in prod; a replacement applications.<app>.analysisTemplates entry named alerts runs in every environment). false opts out; analysis.health.enabled false as well then needs at least one extra template in analysis.templates, because analysis is mandatory for every Rollout.

service.description: The service label the service's Grafana alert rules carry: the lower-cased repository name, or its alias (mycarrier for MC.MyCarrier, curant for MC.Curant). Unset: alerts.serviceName lower-cased, else global.appStack lower-cased (the default app counts as unset). In prod the render fails when none is set.

dryRun.description: Run the alerts metric, and only that metric, in Argo Rollouts dry run: its results are recorded in the AnalysisRun's dryRunSummary and never fail the canary. Set false at go-live. The alert-rules check is always live, whatever this is set to.

interval.description: Time between measurements of the alerts metric.

consecutiveErrorLimit.description: Errors in a row of the alerts metric (a non-2xx answer, a timeout, a connection error, or JSON that is not a list of alerts) that the check tolerates; one more fails the run. A 2xx answer that is not JSON counts as a pass on Argo Rollouts up to v1.10.1.

image.description: Image of the alert-rules Job: Python 3 with its standard library. Set it to a mirror of the default image.

tokenKey.description: Property of the Grafana token under DevOps grafana/service-accounts/api/tokens in Vault.

progressDeadlineSeconds.description: A canary that makes no progress for this long aborts (progressDeadlineAbort is always true).

dark.description: Header-gated dark stage before the weight ladder (Tech Spec D11): canary pods at weight 0, a canary-header route matched on X-MyCarrier-Canary: <global.correlationId>, and the leader's tests-dark suite between the dark-ready and dark-passed barriers. Renders only with the coordinator on. Off by default until the chart renders tests-dark (DEVOPS-326); with true, a tests-dark AnalysisTemplate must render for the leader, or the render fails.

leader.description: The application whose Rollout runs the dark-stage test suite (<environment>-<fullName>-tests-dark). When set, it must name an application of the release; where the dark stage runs (coordinator on, dark true), in every environment, also where the steps do not render, it must be an application with deploymentType rollout and without migratingToRollouts. Required there when the release has more than one such application; a release with one defaults to it.

darkReplicas.description: Canary pods during the dark stage.

bakeMinutes.description: alert-gate's watch window after promotion, in minutes (Tech Spec D18). Rendered on every canary Rollout as the mycarrier.tech/bakeMinutes annotation, which the release's rollout-watch puts in the alert.gate event (DEVOPS-319). Services with a known slow-burn history set a longer window. At most 100: alert-gate's run has activeDeadlineSeconds 7200 and spends about 750 s outside its watch window, so a longer window would be killed before it ends; a value above 100 fails the render.

coordinator.description: Release-wide lockstep through DEVOPS-325's mycarrier/canary-coordinator step plugin (Tech Spec D20). The controller rejects steps for a plugin that is not installed, so a cluster without the plugin needs enabled: false.

enabled.description: Give a preset a start barrier before the ladder (it arms the plugin's Abort hook) and a w<weight> barrier after each weight. An explicit steps list renders verbatim and carries its own barriers. On by default; where the steps render (prod, or stepsOutsideProd) it needs global.correlationId (the pipeline sets it), or every Rollout fails to render. false turns lockstep off, and each Rollout of the release then runs its own steps.

barrierTimeouts.description: Timeout per barrier name; a barrier that times out aborts the Rollout and, through the plugin, its siblings. Each must stay below progressDeadlineSeconds: Argo Rollouts counts the wait at a barrier toward the deadline, and the render fails otherwise.

language.description: Programming language used by the application

disableLanguageSecrets.description: Do not inject the language's default secrets and environment variables (the stack supplies its own)

oneOf.description: Name of the git branch (used for feature branches)
Label for the branch, used for reference label

forceAutoscaling.description: Force autoscaling to be enabled regardless of environment

argoEventsInstance.description: Argo Events namespace the render pipeline runs in. Selects which TestEngine deployment (prod vs dev) receives test trigger payloads.

deploymentStrategy.description: The repository's deployment-strategy property, passed in by chart-renderer. Only the exact string canary gives Rollouts (deploymentType rollout without migratingToRollouts) their canary steps; any other value, or none, renders them without steps and with the same Services, VirtualService and trafficRouting.

name.description: Environment name / namespace (DNS-1123 label). The standard names dev, preprod, prod, qa, uat and feature* have built-in behavior; any other name (e.g. demo) is allowed and treated as a generic environment, so supply its configuration explicitly via global.env / application.env / secrets (the same way qa/uat are configured).

oneOf.description: Override the Kubernetes namespace (defaults to environment.name if not set)
Environment name for dependencies
Whether to override the default domain
Domain to use when override is enabled
Enable Vault CA certificate download during pod startup

BREAK-GLASS ONLY (discouraged): when true, EVERY pod in the release renders WITHOUT runAsNonRoot/securityContext hardening — release-wide, cannot be scoped per-application. The only flag that removes the securityContext hardening block (applications.<name>.enableDebugMode's privileged sidecar is a separate un-hardened-container route). Kyverno require-run-as-non-root backstop is Enforce only on development; production-csp/data run Audit. Not settable via mc-environment environments[]. Leave false/unset; any use must be temporary.

Take over OpenTelemetry configuration from the chart. When true the chart injects no OTEL_* env vars, no auto-instrumentation annotations and no otel-log volume, and overrides disableOtelAutoinstrumentation
Disable the OpenTelemetry Operator's automatic instrumentation (annotations and the nodejs NODE_OPTIONS hook) only; the standard OTEL_* env block is governed by manualOtelConfig
Default tolerations for all applications

isEnvironmentDeploy.description: Whether this is an environment-level deployment. When true, suppresses the offload ApplicationSet generator and enables staticHostname to be added to VirtualService hosts in feature environments.

migration.description: A migrator runs either as a job with timing: pre-deploy, or as a long-running application that runs the migration when it starts and keeps running; as an application it may be deploymentType rollout and then takes part in the canary like any other Rollout (A2). Applications with migration in the name are left out of automatic HPA.

oneOf.description: Whether this is a frontend application
Whether to force offloading

Opt this application's pod template out of Istio sidecar injection and drop the mycarrier.io/gateway annotation (read by _helpers.tpl helm.annotations.istio / helm.annotations.gateway). Not to be confused with service.istioDisabled, which is a separate per-service knob.

Static hostname for the application. In non-feature environments, replaces the default appstack-appname hostname. In feature environments, only added to the VirtualService hosts when isEnvironmentDeploy is true.

Publish the application at the bare apex domain (e.g. mycarriertms.com) with no hostname label, instead of the generated appstack-appname host. Only takes effect in non-feature environments (dev, preprod, prod); ignored in feature environments. Mutually exclusive with staticHostname.
Custom labels to add to the application resources
Custom annotations to add to the application resources

testtrigger.description: Configuration for automated test jobs: an Argo CD PostSync hook Job (<fullName>-trigger) that calls TestEngine after each sync. A Rollout in prod (deploymentType rollout, not migratingToRollouts) gets no hook (Tech Spec D7) only when the repository's deployment-strategy property (global.deploymentStrategy) is canary; with any other value it keeps the hook. Without the hook, with enableV1 (the default) the chart renders the ConfigMap <fullName>-prod-tests (key request.json, the hook's v1 request) and the release's rollout-watch posts it after promotion (DEVOPS-319); with enableV1: false the render fails, because nothing would start its prod tests.

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description: Time to keep test job resources after completion (seconds)

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: Maximum time for the test job to run (seconds)

backoffLimit.description: Number of retries for the test job

apikey.description: API key for the test engine, can be a direct value or a vault reference. For a Rollout in prod whose repository's deployment-strategy property (global.deploymentStrategy) is canary, with enableV1, it must be vault:DevOps/data/testengine/api#encoded_header or unset, or the render fails: rollout-watch posts with that shared key.

resources.description: Resource requests and limits for the test job pod

enableV1.description: When true, all test definitions are bundled into a single curl POST with a {"Tests":[...]} payload sent to the v1 endpoint. When false, each test definition generates a separate curl call to the legacy endpoint, which is retired; true is the default. A Rollout in prod whose repository's deployment-strategy property (global.deploymentStrategy) is canary needs true for its prod tests to run: rollout-watch posts only v1 requests, and the chart renders no hook for it; the render fails with false.

containerImage.description: Container image to use for running tests

secretId.description: Reference to secrets needed for tests, can be a direct value or a vault reference

filters.description: Test filters to select which tests to run. Accepts a single string or an array of strings.

serviceAddress.description: Optional service address for the test to target

additionalEnvVars.description: Additional environment variables to pass to the test container

resultsApiUrl.description: autotest-results-api base URL: a vault reference, or an https URL under mycarrier.tech with no user info, set on the test container as AUTOTEST_RESULTS_API_URL. Set together with resultsApiKey or not at all

resultsApiKey.description: vault reference to the autotest-results-api key (a literal key is refused), set on the test container as AUTOTEST_RESULTS_API_KEY. Set together with resultsApiUrl or not at all

tolerations.description: Tolerations for test pods scheduled by the test engine

nodeAffinity.description: Node affinity rules for test pods scheduled by the test engine

useDefaultNodeAffinity.description: Whether to use default node affinity for test pods. Accepts boolean or string.

spreadAcrossNodes.description: Whether to spread test pods across nodes. Accepts boolean or string.

legacyMode.description: Enable legacy mode for test execution. Accepts boolean or string.

podResources.description: Resource requests and limits for test pods scheduled by the test engine

hardenedSecurityContext.description: Run test pods with a hardened security context (runAsNonRoot + readOnlyRootFilesystem via TestEngine). Accepts boolean or string; only false/"false" opts out.

canaryHealthPath.description: Overrides global.strategy.canary.analysis.health.path for this application: the HTTP path the canary health check calls on its http (or healthcheck) port. Set it for an application whose liveness probe is not HTTP, or one whose health path differs from the stack's or from its liveness path.

progressDeadlineSeconds.description: Overrides global.strategy.canary.progressDeadlineSeconds for this application's Rollout, for an app whose pods take longer to become Ready. Not a step setting, so lockstep is unaffected.

oneOf.description: First release of a two-release switch between Deployment and Rollout, in either direction. The chart renders both workloads: the Rollout references the Deployment through workloadRef (scaleDown: never) with a bare canary strategy, so it takes over no Service, and the HPA/KEDA autoscaler targets the workload deploymentType names. To move to a Rollout, set deploymentType rollout with this flag; to move back, set deploymentType deployment with this flag. Remove it in the next release, once the incoming workload has at least as many ready pods as the outgoing one (with HPA/KEDA, set the autoscaler minimum in release 1 to the outgoing pod count) and, on the way in, the Rollout's availableReplicas equals spec.replicas: Argo CD prunes the other workload, all its pods at once. Never change deploymentType in one release without this flag. See the procedure in values.yaml.
Application version string
Application version as object
Environment variable from source
Image pull policy
Name of the pull secret

command.description: Command to run in the container

args.description: Arguments to pass to the command

subPath.description: Subpath within the volume to mount

configMapName.description: Name of the configMap (if kind is configMap)

items.description: Items to include from the configMap

internalEnabled.description: Enable internal ServiceEntry, WasmPlugin, and VirtualService internal host for feature-routing via WASM fallback. When false, these resources are not rendered and feature-header requests fall through to the default route.

enforceAllowlistOnEnvironmentHeader.description: When an endpoint allowlist applies, the environment-header route has one match per allowed endpoint, so a request that carries the environment header (the frontend and the API gateway send it on every call) meets the allowlist too. false (opt-out) lets the header route match every path, so the allowlist restricts only requests without the header.

externalEnabled.description: Expose the application through the ingress gateway on its public host. When false, its VirtualServices bind only the mesh gateway, keep only the in-mesh hosts (<fullName> and the .internal host) and drop the cloudflare-proxied and mycarrier.io/gateway annotations, so it is reachable only inside the cluster; useRootDomain, staticHostname, networking.istio.hosts and networking.istio.legacyHostAliases then fail the render, as does a frontend application in a multi-frontend release. Set it to false for a migrator Rollout.

offloadVSEnabled.description: Enable the offload VirtualService for feature environments. When false, the offload VS is not rendered for this application.

offloadOperatorEnabled.description: Enable offload-operator managed routing. When true, the standard VirtualService is suppressed and OffloadBase/OffloadRoute CRDs are rendered instead. Does NOT affect the offload VirtualService — that is gated by `offloadVSEnabled`, `networking.krakend.enabled`, and `isEnvironmentDeploy`. Defaults to true when metaEnvironment is dev, false otherwise. Set explicitly to override.

offloadCreationPolicy.description: CreationPolicy for the OffloadBase CRD. Controls how the operator handles the target VirtualService.

offloadVirtualServiceAnnotations.description: Annotations to apply to the operator-managed VirtualService.

offloadVirtualServiceLabels.description: Labels to apply to the operator-managed VirtualService.

gateway.description: Ingress gateway designation (namespace/name) that replaces istio-system/default. The mesh gateway is always included.

routes.description: Custom routes for the VirtualService. Each key is used as the route name. By default, routes destination is the owning application's service. Use the optional 'destination' field to override.

destination.description: Optional destination host override. If not specified, defaults to the owning application's service FQDN.

port.description: Optional destination port override. If not specified, defaults to the application's ports.http value (or 8080).

allowAllEndpoints.description: Dev and feature environments only: skip the endpoint allowlist and route every path to the application, restoring the pre-allowlist behaviour. Setting it to true anywhere else is REJECTED - the render fails rather than ignoring it - because it is a no-op there and the allowlist stays enforced. An explicit false is accepted everywhere. Use when a feature environment needs to serve a path outside /liveness, /health, /api and /swagger; prefer adding that path to allowedEndpoints instead.

allowedEndpoints.description: List of allowed HTTP endpoints for the VirtualService. Can be strings with wildcards or objects with kind and match fields.

oneOf.description: Endpoint path as a string. If it contains *, it will be treated as a prefix match, otherwise as an exact match.
Endpoint definition with explicit kind (prefix, exact, or regex) and match pattern.

kind.description: Type of URI matching: prefix for path prefixes, exact for exact matches, regex for regular expressions.

match.description: The URI pattern to match against incoming requests.

krakend.description: KrakenDAutoConfig CR configuration. When enabled=true the chart renders a gateway.krakend.io/v1alpha1 KrakenDAutoConfig for the application. Requires a non-feature environment, networking.istio.enabled=true, networking.istio.internalEnabled=true, and neither istioDisabled nor service.istioDisabled may be true. See the helm.krakend.enabled helper for the exact gating.

enabled.description: Render a KrakenDAutoConfig CR for this application.

name.description: Override the KrakenDAutoConfig metadata.name. Defaults to <fullName>-autoconfig.

autoConfigNamespace.description: Namespace the KrakenDAutoConfig CR is rendered into. Defaults to gatewayRef.namespace → global.krakendGatewayNamespace → application namespace.

name.description: KrakenDGateway metadata.name to attach generated endpoints to.

namespace.description: Gateway namespace. Falls back to global.krakendGatewayNamespace or the application namespace.

interval.description: Poll interval (Go duration, e.g. 5m). Required when trigger=Periodic.

openapi.description: OpenAPI spec source. By default the URL is auto-generated from the application's `.internal` address using `path`. To bypass auto-generation, set `url` (or `configMapRef`) directly; the supplied value is passed through to the CR.

url.description: Explicit OpenAPI spec URL. When set, overrides the auto-generated http://<app>.<metaEnv>.internal<path> URL. Must point to an internal address (.internal or .svc.cluster.local) and must not contain the external domain.

path.description: Path portion appended to http://<app>.<metaEnv>.internal. Ignored when `url` is set. Defaults to /swagger/v1/swagger.json.

configMapRef.description: Load the OpenAPI spec from a ConfigMap key instead of fetching a URL.

auth.description: Optional authentication configuration for the spec fetch (BearerTokenSecret or BasicAuthSecret).

hostMapping.description: Direct passthrough of KrakenDAutoConfigSpec.urlTransform.hostMapping. Equivalent to extraHostMapping; provided so users can paste rendered CR values verbatim. Each `to:` value must point to an internal address and must not contain the external domain.

extraHostMapping.description: Alias for hostMapping retained for backward compatibility. Entries are appended to any `hostMapping` entries. Each `to:` value must not contain the external domain.

defaults.description: Default values for generated endpoints and backends. Mirrors KrakenDAutoConfigSpec.Defaults.

additionalEndpoints.description: Endpoints not present in the OpenAPI document (e.g. health/liveness probes). Mirrors KrakenDAutoConfigSpec.AdditionalEndpoints. Only `endpoint` is required; `method` (optional, defaults to GET) must be an uppercase CRD enum value; remaining fields are passed through and validated by the operator's CRD and admission webhook.

additionalEndpointsBasePath.description: Overrides the operator's auto-derived base path used to scope additionalEndpoints under the application. Must start with '/'. Mirrors KrakenDAutoConfigSpec.AdditionalEndpointsBasePath.

podDisruptionBudget.description: Optional PodDisruptionBudget for this application. Set exactly one of minAvailable or maxUnavailable. Omit the block entirely to disable (the default).

minAvailable.description: Minimum number (or percentage string like "50%") of pods that must remain available during voluntary disruptions.

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum number (or percentage string like "25%") of pods that may be unavailable during voluntary disruptions.

canary.description: Not supported since mycarrier-helm 4.5.0: canary settings are release-wide in global.strategy.canary (preset, steps, analysis), so every Rollout of a release runs the same steps. The chart refuses to render a Rollout that sets this.

consecutiveErrorLimit.description: Errors in a row the metric tolerates; one more ends the run as Error, which aborts the canary.

provider.description: Exactly one of web (the chart's shorthand for a health-style check: url, statusEndpoint, successCondition, jsonPath, timeoutSeconds; default url is the -preview Service's /health) or job (an Argo Rollouts job provider, passed through; its phase comes from the Job's status). Other metric providers are not supported. The job.container shorthand is no longer supported: canary tests run through TestEngine.

job.description: An Argo Rollouts job provider (metadata, spec), passed through as written.

postStart.description: Command to run on container post-start

preStop.description: Command to run on container pre-stop

preStopSleepSeconds.description: Seconds the container sleeps in a preStop hook before receiving SIGTERM, to allow in-flight requests/sidecars to drain. Defaults to 5 (hook renders by default; see README for grace-period interaction with the chart's default terminationGracePeriodSeconds of 10). Set to 0 to disable the preStop hook entirely.

enabled.description: Enable KEDA ScaledObject for this application

topicName.description: Azure Service Bus topic name (required when type is 'topic')

subscriptionName.description: Azure Service Bus subscription name (required when type is 'topic')

queueName.description: Azure Service Bus queue name (required when type is 'queue')

clusterAuthRef.description: Name of an existing ClusterTriggerAuthentication resource (managed outside this chart). Defaults to servicebus-connectionstring-<env> based on environment (dev/feature -> dev, preprod -> preprod, prod -> prod).

messageCount.description: Target message count per replica to trigger scaling

activationMessageCount.description: Message count threshold to activate the scaler (scale from 0)

pollingInterval.description: How often KEDA checks the trigger source (seconds)

cooldownPeriod.description: Period to wait after last trigger before scaling down (seconds)

idleReplicaCount.description: Number of replicas when idle (set to 0 to enable scale-to-zero)

advanced.description: Advanced KEDA scaling configuration (e.g., scaling policies)

triggers.description: Multiple KEDA triggers for this ScaledObject. Mutually exclusive with the flat type/topicName/subscriptionName/queueName/messageCount/activationMessageCount fields above. minReplicaCount/maxReplicaCount/pollingInterval/cooldownPeriod/idleReplicaCount/advanced remain ScaledObject-level and are not set per-trigger.

topicName.description: Azure Service Bus topic name (required when type is 'topic')

subscriptionName.description: Azure Service Bus subscription name (required when type is 'topic')

queueName.description: Azure Service Bus queue name (required when type is 'queue')

clusterAuthRef.description: Per-trigger override of an existing ClusterTriggerAuthentication resource. Falls back to keda.clusterAuthRef, then to servicebus-connectionstring-<env>.

messageCount.description: Target message count per replica to trigger scaling for this trigger

activationMessageCount.description: Message count threshold to activate this trigger's scaler (scale from 0)

runAsHook.description: With timing, the Job is a real Argo CD hook (pre-deploy: PreSync, post-deploy: PostSync) on its own metadata; a hook runs on every sync (manual, self-heal, each retry), not only when the manifest changes, and Argo CD waits for it. false (opt-out) keeps the Job a plain resource in wave 0, ahead of the workloads, that runs once per manifest change.

successfulJobsHistoryLimit.description: Number of successful jobs to keep in history

failedJobsHistoryLimit.description: Number of failed jobs to keep in history

defaults.description: Default values shared across all Azure Crossplane resources

location.description: Default Azure region for all resources (e.g., 'East US'). Empty string means per-resource location is required.

managementPolicies.description: Crossplane management policies (default: ['Observe']). 'Delete' and '*' (wildcard) are blocked.

managedBy.description: ID of the resource that manages this resource group

namespace.description: Custom Kubernetes namespace (default: environment.name, or environment.namespaceOverride if set)

location.description: Azure region for new storage accounts

name.description: Name for new resource group (auto-generated if omitted)

providerConfigRef.description: Crossplane ProviderConfig name, inherited by all child resources (default: 'default')

capacity.description: Messaging units for Premium SKU (1, 2, 4, 8, or 16)

resourceGroupName.description: Resource group name (default: inf-{env}, e.g. inf-dev)

resourceGroupNameRef.description: Crossplane reference to a ResourceGroup resource

resourceGroupNameSelector.description: Crossplane selector for a ResourceGroup resource

managementPolicies.description: Crossplane management policies (default: ['Observe']). 'Delete' and '*' (wildcard) are blocked.

namespace.description: Custom Kubernetes namespace (default: environment.name, or environment.namespaceOverride if set)

topics.description: Service Bus topics (at least one required)

namespaceId.description: Azure resource ID of the Service Bus namespace

subscriptions.description: Optional topic subscriptions. Omit this field or provide an empty array to create a topic without subscriptions.

alerts.description: Grafana alert rules, contact points and notification route for the stack (see ALERTS.md).

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: Container-level readOnlyRootFilesystem (chart-hardened; unset defaults to true). Set explicitly to false per-workload as a break-glass opt-out. An unconditional /tmp emptyDir is mounted on every workload for temp writes.

fsGroup.description: Pod-level fsGroup (opt-in; unset by default). Must be empty or greater than zero per MyCarrier-DevOps/kyverno-policies `require-non-root-groups` rule `check-fsGroup` — fsGroup 0 is the root group.

type.description: SeccompProfile type, per the Kubernetes SeccompProfile.type API field

localhostProfile.description: Path to a pre-configured profile on the node, relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location. Only used when type is Localhost.

addCapabilities.description: Linux capabilities to add back on top of the drop-all default. All capabilities are dropped by default; list ones here to add them back. Only honoured on the application (Deployment) path by _podsecurity.tpl — jobs and cronjobs do not read this field.
